the staphylococcus species present in feces of the breast-fed infants is different from that present in formula-fed infants.

the staphylococcus species that predominated in the fecal samples of the breast-fed infants was Staphylococcusepidermidis and that the isolates obtained from the feces and the milk were sensitive to most of antibiotics tested.

staphylococcus and enterococcus species were the predominant bacteria in the fecal samples of breast-fed infants, but the staphylococcals strains were less prevalent in the formula-fed infants and the enterococcus faecium was the predominant species among the feces from the formula-fed infants.
